published: 2026-11-09. Published from the private review of 2026-10-25. Agent review receipt identifiers were removed; every measurement, identity hash, correctness result and guard result is unchanged. Companion: 2026-10-25-exl3-prototype.md.
decision: Do not undertake full EXL3 runtime port for speed on current evidence. Correct bounded prototype is slower; no claim that the format is intrinsically slow.

exl3.scope: Actual packed operators with synthetic activations; no full-model or GGUF speed claim.
exl3.timing_scope: Resident weights/pipeline; all calls include transforms and synchronization. fused_reuse and nmajor variants reuse scratch/output; other paths allocate each call. Python dispatch remains included.
exl3.event_timing: Not collected. Optional torch.mps.Event diagnostics were removed after the installed Torch 2.14.1 elapsed-time wait hung. Wall measurements are not pure GPU kernel durations.
exl3.cache_treatment: Before every timed call, multiply a separate reusable FP32 MPS buffer and synchronize outside the stopwatch. This applies cache pressure; it does not prove a perfectly cold cache.

limitations: EXL3 uses three Python-submitted kernels and FP16 I/O; GGML uses a resident C++ graph and F32 I/O. Complete call timings, not pure device kernel times.
128 MiB read/write cache pressure is not proof of perfectly cold caches.
Different model weights; each was verified against its own decoded-weight oracle. No quality equivalence or whole-model speed claim.
MPS event elapsed_time stalled in installed Torch; supervised attempt cancelled cleanly. Subsequent wall-only run completed.
GGUF runs were too short for meaningful sampled peak RSS; graph allocation bytes are recorded.
